proposed_from.topic: Two-resolution minimax and honest-band frontier for distribution-valued regression discontinuity under sparse within-unit sampling. Observe n independent aggregate units with a sharp cutoff treatment, a latent potential outcome distribution on [0,1], and m conditionally iid subunit draws. On the fixed beta-smooth latent-density, gamma-smooth scalar-pushforward, and s-smooth cutoff-regression class in the strongest-form draft, determine matching minimax sup-norm risk and all-honest simultaneous-band width for the local average quantile treatment-effect curve over every joint n,m regime: a positive bounded-m floor, the sharp intermediate frontier, and the smallest m_crit recovering dense-oracle R3D. Construct a cross-y-compatible estimator and bias-aware studentized simultaneous band. Consumer: R3D::r3d and the CPS state-income application. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The conditional Beta/order-statistic operator and a full/half-sample jackknife give bias O(m^{-r}), r=min((beta+1)/2,2), and the upper rate n^{-s/(2s+1)}+m^{-r}. Smooth moment-matched latent laws give exact complete-tuple equivalence for fixed m. A hidden-label spectral divergence calculation plus a beta=3/2 quantile cusp yields a candidate polynomial m^{-4-2gamma} floor; normalization, support-edge, signed-weight, covariance, and direct-collision checks found no fatal defect. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a sharp complete-observation modulus matching an attainable compatible-estimator upper bound throughout the intermediate regimes. EARLY KILL TEST: Certify the gamma-normalized beta=3/2 cusp and complete-tuple divergence inside the fixed class constants; stop or pivot if no bounded replacement survives. seed_details.title: Complete-tuple two-resolution modulus for the local average quantile treatment-effect curve
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the empirical-quantile assumptions and Proposition on empirical quantiles, and the conclusion
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace oracle negligibility of empirical quantiles by a direct modulus analysis for the conditional \(m\)-tuple experiment before applying one-sided cutoff localization.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for sparse Wasserstein barycenter minimax rates, grouped-observation average-quantile rates, and distribution-valued regression discontinuity found Peng et al. (2026), Vinayak et al. (2019), and functional-data phase-transition papers, but no matching nonparametric LAQTE modulus.
seed_details.novelty_check: The exact target--method pair is unoccupied: the same LAQTE appears only under oracle inner sampling, while the complete-tuple papers target unconditional barycenters, finite mixtures, or the full scalar mixing law.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate from Berger et al. (2025) after replacing grid size by \(m\). Rebuttal: their additive noisy-grid experiment is identified at every fixed grid, whereas the latent-distribution tuple operator has nontrivial fibers and a nonlinear average-quantile functional.

seed_details.title: Minimax all-honest simultaneous-band width across sparse, intermediate, and oracle regimes
seed_details.anchor_location: The multiplier-bootstrap theorem and empirical-quantile corollary
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace bootstrap centering under negligible inner error by a two-component bias allowance and an ordered-modulus lower bound for the complete tuple law.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for honest Wasserstein-barycenter bands and sparse distribution-valued RD bands found Armstrong and Kolesar (2018), Cai and Hu (2025), and Peng et al. (2026), but no minimax simultaneous-width result for the LAQTE curve.
seed_details.novelty_check: The exact honest-width target is unoccupied because nearby bands either assume additive measurements, scalar outcomes, parametric mixing laws, or oracle inner resolution.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: Cai and Hu (2025) already give bands from sparse to dense functional sampling. Rebuttal: their additive measurement model has a variance phase transition but no finite-resolution identification floor or boundary-RD bias.

seed_details.title: Uniform intermediate-regime law for a correction-and-projection compatible estimator
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Propositions on bias-corrected distribution and quantile processes, split-panel jackknife construction, and conclusion
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Derive the noisy-quantile expansion conditionally on a latent distribution and uniformly in quantile index, then differentiate monotone projection when inner and outer errors have the same order.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for sparse barycenter Gaussian processes and projection-compatible quantile correction found Peng et al. (2026) and Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val, and Galichon (2010), but their limit laws assume either a parametric marginal model or a preliminary functional central limit theorem.
seed_details.novelty_check: No closer paper derives the preliminary complete-tuple functional process under signed boundary weights when the correction and RD errors collide.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: rearrangement preserves first-order laws by Chernozhukov et al. (2010). Rebuttal: that paper starts from a functional central limit theorem and does not derive one for complete grouped samples with signed boundary weights and first-order inner bias.

seed_details.title: Local asymptotic efficiency envelope for sparse barycenter regression at a cutoff
seed_details.anchor_location: Asymptotic treatment-effect theorem and empirical-quantile extension
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the oracle influence process by a tangent-space calculation through the \(m\)-tuple mixture operator.
seed_details.destination_search: A targeted search for semiparametric efficiency of sparse Wasserstein barycenters found no exact result, but the fixed-\(m\) target is nonidentified and the growing-\(m\) experiment is nonregular.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: an efficiency bound is undefined when fixed \(m\) leaves the target unidentified. Rebuttal fails for the all-regime target; an efficiency analysis would require a different regularized estimand.

seed_details.title: If-and-only-if characterization of functionals constant on grouped-sample operator fibers
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the \(V_m\) operator, sharp identification theorems, tensor proof construction, and discussion
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace finite-component tensor uniqueness by annihilator duality for linear functionals of a continuous mixing law.
seed_details.destination_search: Peng et al. (2026) now establish bounded-sample nonidentification and a marginal representation, but do not characterize every continuous-mixing functional constant on the complete-tuple fibers.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: the answer is merely the span of degree-\(m\) product moments. Rebuttal: proving necessity under compatible CDF paths and translating that annihilator into an evaluable average-quantile criterion is not supplied by grouped finite-mixture theory.

seed_details.title: Leverage-adjusted effective resolution for heterogeneous cell sizes and survey weights
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, local REM construction, Theorem 2 proof decomposition, implementation, and discussion
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the common inner sample size in the conditional order-statistic expansion by a weighted operator whose singular values depend jointly on cell precision and RD leverage.
seed_details.destination_search: Zhou and Muller (2024) treat heterogeneous counts through an additional empirical-measure error, and Jochmans and Weidner (2024) permit heterogeneous precision, but neither identifies the effective resolution for a cutoff average-quantile curve.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: the harmonic mean of cell sizes is the answer. Rebuttal: signed one-sided local-polynomial leverage and nonlinear quantiles can make two designs with the same harmonic mean have different complete-experiment information.

seed_details.title: Actual estimand and correction frontier of empirical-quantile R3D
seed_details.anchor_location: Empirical-quantile estimator, Proposition on empirical quantiles, and its proof
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Diagonalize the conditional order-statistic operator before the RD smoother and expose its quantile-index weight map.
seed_details.destination_search: The order-statistic identity is explicit in Peng et al. (2026), while Jochmans and Weidner (2024) give generic noisy-proxy jackknifing; the remaining contribution would be the exact R3D operator frontier and compatible correction.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate from the Bernstein--Durrmeyer expansion and a half-sample jackknife. Rebuttal: that objection defeats the bias formula alone, but not the complete-tuple regularization frontier; the seed is therefore absorbed by the stronger modulus project.

seed_details.title: Critical inner-resolution curve for sign-robust LAQTE conclusions
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, ordered-modulus construction, optimal confidence-interval theorem, and RD application
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Augment worst-case cutoff bias by the complete-tuple identification radius and solve for the smallest \(m\) at which zero leaves the simultaneous band.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper found a critical finite-resolution curve for distribution-valued RD, but the object is application-dependent unless coupled to the global minimax modulus.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: the critical value is just estimated effect divided by a bias bound. Rebuttal: the complete-tuple bias radius is itself unknown; once derived, however, this seed becomes a corollary rather than an independent kernel.

seed_details.title: Policy regret from local distribution-valued discontinuities
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Convert a cutoff-local LAQTE curve into welfare scores for a policy class.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found Safe Policy Learning under Regression Discontinuity Designs and Wasserstein Policy Learning for Distributional Outcomes (2026).
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: a single cutoff identifies only a local effect and cannot rank policies away from the cutoff. The objection holds without multiple cutoffs or transport restrictions, and the destination pair is already occupied.

seed_details.title: Permutation-inverted finite-sample bands for a distribution-valued cutoff effect
seed_details.anchor_location: Uniform local-Wald process and multiplier inference for quantile RD
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Find a valid symmetry orbit for the cutoff contrast before inverting a quantile-process score.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found conformal distributional prediction and approximate permutation tests for RD covariate continuity, but no exchangeability theorem for the causal LAQTE jump.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: deterministic threshold assignment supplies no finite-sample treatment-label exchangeability. The objection holds under the maintained continuity design, so conformal inversion would require a different local-randomization model.
